name: September 2026 · International · Version 3 · Reading & Writing
description: Full-length SAT Reading & Writing from the September 2026 exam · 2 modules × 27 = 54 questions. 27 questions that could not be read from the source scan are filled in from the Humo AI question bank.

questions.passage: In 1877, 85% of California’s railways were already controlled by the Southern Pacific Railroad. The company further solidified its ______ in rail access to the state’s Pacific coast when it completed the Sunset Route in 1883: running from Louisiana to Southern California, the route established the first transcontinental rail line across the southern United States.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: dominance
creativity
insignificance
neutrality
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A.

The researchers suspect that video meeting participants are focused on staring at the speaker on the screen and don’t allow their eyes or mind to wander as much, which may ultimately ______ creativity.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: recommend
criticize
impede
construct
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C.

Stephens and colleagues claim that this extended period could be ______ the relatively small pool of potential pollinators available to zygomorphic flowers and the greater chance at successful pollination that remaining open affords them.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: analogous to
converted by
attributed to
magnified by

questions.passage: The following text is adapted from Louisa May Alcott’s 1869 novel An Old-Fashioned Girl. Polly, a teenager, is visiting her friend Fanny. Fanny’s friends did not interest Polly much; she was rather afraid of them [because] they seemed so much older and wiser than herself, even those younger in years. They talked about things of which she knew nothing and when Fanny tried to explain, she didn’t find them interesting; indeed, some of them rather shocked and puzzled her.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To portray Polly’s reaction to Fanny’s friends
To identify the topics Polly talks about with Fanny’s friends
To explain how Fanny met some of her friends
To illustrate how Fanny’s friends feel about Polly

questions.passage: In ancient Egypt, beer was not just a drink for special occasions. It was part of everyday life for people of all classes. Workers who built monuments often received beer as part of their daily pay, along with bread. Egyptian beer was thick and only mildly alcoholic, and it provided calories and nutrients that helped sustain people doing hard physical labor. Records show that beer was also offered to the gods during temple ceremonies.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It describes the steps ancient Egyptians followed to brew beer.
It argues that beer was more valuable to workers than bread.
It offers a reason that beer was a useful part of the pay workers received.
It shows that beer was reserved mainly for religious ceremonies.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is C.

questions.passage: Morocco has long imported most of the fuel it uses to make electricity. To change this, the country built one of the world's largest solar power complexes near the desert city of Ouarzazate. Part of the complex uses curved mirrors to focus sunlight and heat a fluid. Some of that heat is stored in tanks of melted salt, allowing the plant to keep producing electricity for hours after sunset. Projects like this one are helping Morocco rely more on its own abundant sunshine.
questions.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe a project Morocco built to generate electricity from sunlight, including how it keeps working after dark
To argue that every country should build large solar power plants
To explain why deserts receive more sunlight than other regions
To compare Morocco's fuel imports with those of neighboring countries
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A.

questions.passage:
Text 1
To save money, some rural school districts have switched to a four-day school week. District leaders point out that closing buildings one day a week reduces spending on heating, transportation, and support staff, and they argue that these savings help keep their districts financially stable.

Text 2
An analysis of districts that adopted four-day weeks found that the savings were modest, usually around 1 to 2 percent of a district's budget. The analysis also noted that many families had to pay for childcare on the fifth day, an added cost that did not appear in any district budget.
questions.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the district leaders' argument in Text 1?
options: By claiming that families save money when schools close one day a week
By suggesting that the savings are smaller than the leaders imply and that some costs are shifted to families
By agreeing that four-day weeks greatly increase the amount of money in district budgets
By arguing that heating and transportation have no effect on school spending
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B.

questions.passage:
Text 1
In Hindustani classical music of northern India, many ragas (melodic frameworks) are traditionally assigned to particular times of day—some to dawn, others to late night. Musicologist Arjun Mehta argues that these assignments should be respected because they connect each raga to the mood of its hour and are an essential part of the tradition.

Text 2
Concert organizer Kavita Rao notes that most public concerts today take place in the evening, when audiences are free. If performers followed the time-of-day rules strictly, she observes, morning ragas would almost never be heard in concert halls. Rao suggests that performers sometimes play morning ragas in the evening so that audiences can still experience them.
questions.question: Based on the texts, how would Rao (Text 2) most likely respond to Mehta's argument in Text 1?
options: She would suggest that following the time-of-day rules strictly could keep audiences from hearing some ragas.
She would argue that ragas are not actually linked to particular times of day.
She would agree that morning ragas should never be performed in the evening.
She would claim that most concerts in northern India take place in the morning.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A.

questions.passage: Navigators in the Marshall Islands of the central Pacific traditionally made charts from strips of palm rib tied together, with small shells marking the locations of islands. Unlike most maps, these stick charts did not mainly show coastlines or distances. Instead, the curved and straight sticks represented patterns of ocean swells—the way waves bend and cross as they meet islands. Navigators studied the charts on land and memorized them; they generally did not bring the charts on voyages, relying instead on feeling the swells through the hull of the canoe.
questions.question: Based on the text, which statement about Marshall Islands stick charts is true?
options: They were carried on every voyage so that navigators could consult them at sea.
They mainly showed coastlines and the exact distances between islands.
They were made from strips of metal and pieces of stone.
They represented patterns of ocean swells and were studied before voyages.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D.

questions.passage: Onggi, the large earthenware jars traditionally used in Korea to ferment and store foods such as kimchi and soy sauce, are prized for a quality that potters describe as "breathing." The clay contains tiny pores that let air pass slowly through the jar's walls while keeping liquids inside. This gentle exchange of air helps foods ferment evenly and keeps them from spoiling, which is why many Korean families still use onggi even though modern refrigerators are widely available.
questions.question: According to the text, why do many Korean families still use onggi?
options: Onggi cost less than modern refrigerators do.
The jars' porous walls help foods ferment well and keep them from spoiling.
The jars are completely airtight, so they seal in the foods' flavor.
Onggi must be used at certain family celebrations.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B.

questions.passage: Animals use many objects as tools to achieve goals more easily. Such goals include grooming, finding food, and protecting themselves. For a long time, people thought tool use was unique to primates. Octopuses and other animals, though, have busted the myth that tool use requires hands. Inventively, octopuses use two halves of a seashell to provide protection or a place to hide. Palm cockatoos also get creative. They use leaves to pad their beaks when opening nuts.
questions.question: According to the text, what do octopuses use to protect themselves?
options: Sand
Leaves
Two halves of a seashell
Feathers from palm cockatoos

questions.passage: In Switzerland, the white fuzzy mountain flowers known as edelweiss are widely treated as a symbol of strength and courage. Although edelweiss can thrive in extreme conditions, they aren’t notably tougher or harder to reach than other mountain flowers growing in the Swiss Alps. Historian Tobias Scheidegger has shown that the popular view of the flowers originated in the mid-1800s when mountain climbing became popular in Switzerland. Mountain climbers spread the idea that the flowers grew only in steep, icy terrains that were dangerous to climb to. Scheidegger says that these claims were self-interested. He suggests that mountain climbers presented edelweiss in this way in order to ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: make themselves appear brave and strong for being able to climb to difficult places where edelweiss supposedly grew.
encourage more flower enthusiasts to explore the Swiss Alps.
share their observations about the unusual characteristics of edelweiss with scientists.
prove that edelweiss were more common in the Swiss Alps than in other mountain regions in Europe.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A.

questions.passage: In China, collectors often stamped their personal seals directly onto paintings they owned. A Qing dynasty landscape scroll now in a museum in Taipei bears the seals of seven collectors. Art historian Liu Wen explains that early owners of a scroll usually placed their seals in open areas close to the painted image; as those spaces filled up, later owners had to squeeze their seals into the scroll's margins. On this scroll, three seals are crowded into the margins. Those three seals most likely ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: belong to owners who acquired the scroll after the owners whose seals appear close to the image.
were stamped by the artist who painted the scroll.
belong to the scroll's earliest owners.
were added to cover damage to the painted image.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is A.

they
it

In comparison,
Firstly,
In conclusion,

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Spiders are classified as arachnids.
  • There are other types of arachnids besides spiders.
  • Harvestmen are a type of arachnid.
  • Harvestmen are also known as daddy longlegs.
  • Harvestmen are not spiders.
questions.question: The student wants to explain what harvestmen are. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Spiders, also known as harvestmen, are classified as arachnids.
There are other types of arachnids besides spiders, such as daddy longlegs.
The spiders known as daddy longlegs are classified as harvestmen.
Harvestmen, also known as daddy longlegs, are arachnids but not spiders.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is D.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • Zaï is a farming technique used in Burkina Faso and other parts of West Africa's Sahel region.
  • Farmers dig small pits in hard, dry soil before the rainy season.
  • They fill the pits with manure or compost.
  • The pits catch rainwater and hold it near the plants' roots.
  • Zaï can greatly increase yields of crops such as sorghum and millet.
questions.question: The student wants to explain how zaï helps plants get water. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Zaï, a technique used in Burkina Faso, can greatly increase yields of crops such as sorghum and millet.
Zaï pits catch rainwater and hold it near the plants' roots.
Before the rainy season, farmers using zaï dig small pits in hard, dry soil.
Farmers using zaï fill small pits with manure or compost.
questions.explanation: The correct answer is B.

Al-Sweedan and Moath Alhaj recently chose the novel path of focusing on people who live below sea level, in locations such as the California towns of Salton City and Coachella.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: eccentric
meager
conventional
random
questions.explanation: The researchers took a “novel path” that differs from the typical studies, so those studies are “conventional.”

questions.passage: Parapuzosia seppenradensis, known to have lived in what is now Mexico, and Parapuzosia leptophylla, known to have lived in what is now England, were both ammonites, but P. seppenradensis was much larger than P. leptophylla. Recent research by Christina Ifrim, Nils Schorndorf, and colleagues has suggested that this ______ resulted from the unique predator threat faced by each species.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: disparity
enmity
anomaly
ambiguity
questions.explanation: The text describes a difference in size between the two species, a “disparity.”

questions.passage:
The following text is adapted from Yone Noguchi’s 1914 memoir The Story of Yone Noguchi. Noguchi is returning home after eleven years abroad.

I reached Tsushima, my native town, at evening.

I frightened my old father at the station, who was actually trying to find me among some other people. There is no wonder that he could not recognise me; I must have changed a great deal.
questions.question: As used in the text, what does the word “find” most nearly mean?
options: Locate
Reveal
Persuade
Embarrass
questions.explanation: His father was trying to spot, or locate, him among the crowd.

questions.passage: In addition to the giant stock exchanges in places like London, Mumbai, and Tokyo, there are many smaller exchanges such as the Beirut Stock Exchange in Beirut, Lebanon. Though small, by being dedicated to Lebanon, it can better address factors that help local businesses ______, and that focus on the success of local businesses benefits investors and the local economy.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
options: thrive
disperse
ebb
overspend
questions.explanation: Factors that help businesses and benefit the economy help them “thrive.”

questions.passage: Researchers César A. Hidalgo, Elisa Castañer, and Andres Sevtsuk created a computer model to predict the mix of movie theaters, gyms, and other businesses found in a given neighborhood. How we define a neighborhood and its boundaries is subjective, so the team used a clustering algorithm to locate dense groupings of amenities that represent human-identified neighborhoods like Boston’s Harvard Square. The predictive model, which incorporates this algorithm, is sure to be invaluable in determining the optimal mix of a city’s amenities.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It praises an algorithm’s accuracy in identifying neighborhood boundaries.
It emphasizes the potential utility of the team’s model.
It suggests a difficulty associated with analyzing neighborhoods that the research team attempted to overcome.
It summarizes trends in recent urban development in Boston.
questions.explanation: The sentence says the model will be “invaluable,” which stresses its potential usefulness.

questions.passage: Asteroid 6478 Gault has experienced intermittent mass loss since at least 2013, but in contrast to some other asteroids with repeated mass-loss episodes, 6478 Gault has not lost mass at its perihelion (the closest point of its orbit to the Sun), and thus the loss is not attributable to solar energy-driven ice vaporization. And as Jane X. Luu et al. point out, the singular nature of impact ejection makes it untenable as an account of multiple loss episodes of similar duration over several years. Instead, Luu et al. are likely correct that 6478 Gault is shedding mass due to rotational instability.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It presents a scientific observation, describes a contrast between that observation and other observations, and then explains why those other observations should not be considered credible.
It describes an astronomical finding, discusses competing theories about that finding that the author regards as flawed, and then describes new evidence that supports an alternative theory.
It discusses a physical process, evaluates possible causes of that process, and then states that a persuasive account of the process has yet to be put forward.
It introduces a natural phenomenon, refutes two potential explanations for that phenomenon, and then presents a third explanation for that phenomenon that the author regards as plausible.
questions.explanation: The text rules out ice vaporization and impact ejection, then favors rotational instability.

questions.passage: Community science, which involves professional scientists collaborating with amateur science enthusiasts to study a topic, is often an effective and engaging way to conduct research. It can allow people to assist with conservation efforts, provide youth with learning experiences outside of the classroom, and increase the amount of data researchers can collect. This approach was essential to the success of a study by biologist Grace Herzel and colleagues of butterfly color and its relation to behavior, which included findings from hundreds of students and community members in northwestern Arkansas.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It argues for a new approach to scientific research, comments on the public’s opinion about the approach, and then describes how that approach was applied in a certain study.
It introduces the topic of a scientific study, describes the study’s importance, and then presents the study’s results.
It describes the development of a type of scientific collaboration, shows how that type of collaboration has been used in a particular field of study, and then suggests future collaborative projects.
It identifies a particular approach to research, lists some benefits of that approach, and then mentions a study in which that approach was used.
questions.explanation: The text names community science, lists its benefits, and then cites the Herzel study.

questions.passage:
Text 1

Death Cab for Cutie’s 2003 song “Lightness” includes a specific musical pattern. That pattern consists of two alternating notes sung over and over with “wa” and “oh” sounds, resulting in a sequence of “Wa-oh-wa-oh.” This pattern showed up in so many pop songs in the 2000s and 2010s that eventually it earned a nickname, “the millennial whoop.” Unfortunately, the whoop showed up so frequently that it could be more irritating than enjoyable.

Text 2

The millennial whoop could be annoying. Not every pop song needs “Wa-oh-wa-ohs!” and it seemed as though nearly every pop song released between 2000 and 2017 had them. But the whoop could also be genuinely fun or even moving. Too many songwriters used it in too many pop songs for a time, but that doesn’t mean the whoop was never used well.
questions.question: Which choice best describes the relationship between the perspectives provided in Text 1 and Text 2?
options: Text 1 provides an explanation of events that inspired a song, while Text 2 offers a different explanation of those events.
Text 1 discusses the advantages of a technique for recording music, while Text 2 discusses the problems with that technique.
Text 1 introduces a negative view of a musical pattern, while Text 2 presents a more positive view of that pattern.
Text 1 focuses on critics who praised a particular style of music, while Text 2 focuses on critics who disapproved of that style.
questions.explanation: Text 1 calls the whoop irritating; Text 2 admits it was overused but says it could be fun or moving.

questions.passage: Why do flat-headed cats purr but jaguars roar? Researchers hypothesize that this difference between the two feline species may be partly due to a U-shaped bone in their throats called the hyoid. Flat-headed cats, which are much smaller than jaguars, have a rigid hyoid that rumbles when the cat’s larynx vibrates, resulting in a purr. By contrast, jaguars have a somewhat flexible hyoid, and the bone is attached to the skull with a stretchy ligament that flat-headed cats lack. These traits allow jaguars and most other species of big cats to produce powerful roars. The same traits may also prevent most big cats from purring.
questions.question: According to the text, which trait do researchers think may contribute to a flat-headed cat’s ability to purr?
options: The shape of the flat-headed cat’s larynx
The ligament attaching the hyoid bone to the flat-headed cat’s skull
The flat-headed cat’s rigid hyoid bone
The relative size of the flat-headed cat’s body and throat
questions.explanation: The text says a rigid hyoid rumbles when the larynx vibrates, producing a purr.

questions.passage: Memoirs of Elleanor Eldridge is an 1838 historical account by Elleanor Eldridge and Frances Harriet Whipple Green. In the book, the authors assert that people don’t need to be famous to be worthy of memoirs, writing,
questions.question: Which quotation from Memoirs of Elleanor Eldridge most effectively illustrates the claim?
options: “Then let no one turn with too much [fussiness] from the simple story of the humble Elleanor, though it may contain few, or none, of the thrilling charms of poetry and passion.”

“There is often a kind of [deceptive] light, playing around such [famous] names, calculated to dazzle and mislead, by their false lustre, until the eye can no longer receive the pure light of Truth, or the mind appreciate real excellence, or intrinsic worth.”
“It should not be considered essential to the interest and value of biography, that its subject be of exalted rank, or illustrious name.”

“How careful ought we to be to speak nothing but the truth, even in regard to the most trifling circumstances; and not only so, but to be well assured that what we suppose to be true, is truth, before we receive it as such.”
questions.explanation: Only C says a subject need not have exalted rank or an illustrious name to be worth a biography.

questions.passage: A student is writing a research paper on the history of irrigation in the United States, situating the development of the Bear River Reservoir (created in Amador County, California, in 1900) in a larger historical context. The student claims that innovation in irrigation practices throughout the United States has led to designs with increased efficiency.
questions.question: Which quotation from a study of irrigation best supports the student’s claim?
options: “While the low humidity of Southern California’s desert areas makes irrigation a requirement if agriculture is to be a success there, the relatively high humidity in the northern parts of the state makes such practices less necessary.”

“The importance of irrigation infrastructure in the United States today cannot be overstated, since it is the most widely utilized means of conveying water for food production. Accordingly, any increase in the efficiency of irrigation, however small, would be of significant economic and social value.”
“The irrigation system developed by the Hohokam people in the 7th century CE in what is now Arizona was simple but applied hydraulic engineering design features that are still in use today.”

“Competition for water as a scarce economic resource inspired the development of sprinkler irrigation systems, which have contributed to the reduction of water used for irrigation in the United States to 45% of the total water usage of its population. Comparatively, 70% of the world’s water usage is dedicated to irrigation.”
questions.explanation: Only D describes an innovation (sprinkler systems) that made irrigation more efficient by reducing the water used.

questions.passage: Studying animals in a laboratory allows variables to be systematically controlled, but removing animals from their wild habitats can affect their behavior and biology in unforeseen ways. Given this, biologists Rebecca M. Calisi-Rodriguez and George E. Bentley examined research on brown-throated three-toed sloths and canaries to see whether results from studies in the wild were consistent with the results of studies in the laboratory. Therefore, data showing that brown-throated three-toed sloths tend to sleep fewer than 10 hours per day in the wild would be irrelevant to Calisi-Rodriguez and Bentley’s investigation if ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: this behavior pattern has not been studied in the lab.
they tend to sleep more than 15 hours per day in the lab.
the brains of male canaries show predictable seasonal changes in the wild.
such data have been collected for canaries in laboratory settings but not in the wild.
questions.explanation: Wild data can only be compared with lab data if the lab data exist; without lab studies of sloth sleep, the wild data would be irrelevant to the comparison.

questions.passage: Carl Woese’s 1970s study of methanogens (microbes with no nuclei, such as Methanococcus vannielii, that metabolize hydrogen and carbon dioxide in oxygen-poor environments and produce methane as a by-product) suggested that they did not fit scientists’ then-conventional division of life into two domains, the eukaryotes (having cells with nuclei) and the prokaryotes (missing nuclei). Molecular clock evidence indicated that what Woese argued was a third domain of life emerged as early as 3.5 billion years ago. Methanogens would have been well-adapted to conditions then given that ______
questions.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?
options: atmospheric hydrogen levels were much lower around 3.3 billion years ago than they were both earlier and later in Earth’s history.
methane, while primarily biological in origin on Earth, can be produced in the absence of biological activity.
the earliest undisputed evidence of eukaryotes is much more recent than 3.5 billion years ago.
Earth’s oxygen levels were very low until the Great Oxidation Event approximately 2.4 billion years ago.
questions.explanation: Methanogens thrive in oxygen-poor environments, and Earth had very little oxygen until about 2.4 billion years ago, so they were well suited to early Earth.

questions.passage: The Southern Delta Aquariid meteor shower has a zenithal hourly rate (ZHR) of 25, meaning that at the shower’s peak, 25 meteors per hour could potentially be seen by a hypothetical observer. A calculation that assumes ideal viewing conditions, ______
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: an actual viewer’s observed number of meteors in an hour and the ZHR may differ considerably.
the number of meteors an actual viewer observes in an hour may differ considerably from the ZHR.
there may be a considerable difference between the number of meteors an actual viewer observes in an hour and the ZHR.
the ZHR may differ considerably from the number of meteors an actual viewer observes in an hour.
questions.explanation: The opening phrase “A calculation that assumes ideal viewing conditions” describes the ZHR, so “the ZHR” must come next.

questions.passage: Jordan’s constitution, enacted in 1952, contains just one of the six constitutional features that enhance judicial independence, as identified by legal scholars James Melton and Tom Ginsburg. After 1985, such de jure judicial independence became more prevalent, as exemplified in Croatia’s constitution, enacted in 1991 and ______ four of these features.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: contained
containing
had contained
contains
questions.explanation: “enacted in 1991 and containing four of these features” keeps the two participles parallel.

questions.passage: Many Farms Chapter, which covers 168,000 acres, is one of the 110 chapters of the Navajo ______ Diné bizaad (the Navajo language), the chapter is called Da’ak’eh Halani.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Nation, in
Nation. In
Nation and in
Nation in
questions.explanation: Two complete sentences need a period between them: “…Navajo Nation. In Diné bizaad, the chapter is called…”

questions.passage: After finding information about Ronald V. Dellums, who represented California in the United States House of Representatives, the student discovered biographical sketches of two other Black Americans who served in ______ Ralph Harold Metcalfe of Illinois and George Henry White of North Carolina.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Congress.
Congress:
Congress;
Congress
questions.explanation: A colon correctly introduces the two names after a complete clause.

questions.passage: While the greater adjutant (Leptoptilos dubius) can be found in places like the Inner Gulf of Thailand and Manchar Lake in ______ than 80 percent of this endangered stork species is found in Assam, India. There, wildlife biologist Dr. Purnima Devi Barman is on the front lines of conservation efforts to bring adjutants back from near extinction.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Pakistan, more
Pakistan; more
Pakistan. More
Pakistan more
questions.explanation: The introductory “While…” clause is followed by a comma before the main clause.

questions.passage: The World Cup of men’s soccer, one of the biggest sporting events on the planet, brought 32 national teams from six continents to the host country, Qatar, in 2022. The event, which is held every four years, used to be much smaller and more limited geographically. ______ the 1950 World Cup in Brazil included only 13 teams, all from Europe and the Americas.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: In addition,
However,
At last,
For example,
questions.explanation: The 1950 tournament is an example of the earlier, smaller events.

questions.passage: Since 1941, the South Side Community Art Center in Chicago, Illinois, has cultivated a multigenerational community of Black creatives—from writer Gwendolyn Brooks, to musician Nat King Cole, to visual artists like Eldzier Cortor and Barbara Jones-Hogu. ______ it has garnered a reputation as a hub of Black art and culture in Chicago.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: On the other hand,
Nevertheless,
Periodically,
Accordingly,
questions.explanation: Its reputation follows from the community it cultivated, so “Accordingly.”

questions.passage: Scientists long debated the origins of chondrules, tiny glass beads that formed in meteors billions of years ago. For decades, different theories were proposed, from lightning strikes to powerful rock collisions, but none had sufficient evidentiary support. ______ scientists found strong evidence that chondrules were formed by shock waves in nearby nebulae.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: For example,
Finally,
Similarly,
Therefore,
questions.explanation: After decades of failed theories, strong evidence arrived at last, so “Finally.”

questions.passage: The star Wezen is unvaryingly bright, consistently ranking as one of the brightest stars in the sky (Wezen ranked 36th on a recent list). By contrast, the brightness of the red giant Betelgeuse varies considerably. Indeed, between April and June 2023, Betelgeuse became an astonishing 40% brighter; ______ its ranking rose from 10th to 7th.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: in sum,
in turn,
specifically,
for example,
questions.explanation: The ranking change gives the specific detail of the 40% brightening, so “specifically.”

questions.passage: For several centuries after the birth of opera in sixteenth-century Florence, Italian remained the default language in which most opera scores were written. ______ opera singers today, such as the tenor Lawrence Brownlee, encounter a wide range of Italian terms—from affettuoso (with feeling) to affrettando (at a hurried tempo)—when following many eighteenth-century opera scores.
questions.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
options: Hence,
Lastly,
Granted,
However,
questions.explanation: Italian being the default language leads to today’s singers meeting Italian terms, so “Hence.”

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Leidenfrost effect occurs when liquid touches a solid surface significantly hotter than the liquid’s boiling point, forming a vapor layer that insulates the liquid before eventually collapsing.
  • Scientists long hypothesized that the temperatures at which Leidenfrost vapor forms and collapses vary depending on molecular variations in surfaces and liquids.
  • A 2023 study confirmed that the vapor’s formation temperature varies depending on molecular variations in surfaces and liquids.
  • The study also found that the vapor’s collapse temperature was “nearly independent of material and fluid properties,” contrary to previous theories.
  • The vapor’s collapse temperature remained consistent (around 140°C).
questions.question: The student wants to refute a scientific assumption about the Leidenfrost effect. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Though the vapor layer created by the Leidenfrost effect can be formed at a range of temperatures, the temperature at which the layer collapses varies depending on material and fluid properties.

Scientists had hypothesized that the formation temperature of Leidenfrost vapor depends on variations in surfaces and liquids used, but a 2023 study confirmed that the collapse temperature remains consistent.
Countering previous hypotheses, a recent study found that Leidenfrost vapor’s collapse temperature does not vary depending on material and fluid properties.

Contrary to the hypothesis that vapor layer formation temperature is dictated by molecular variation, a 2023 study confirmed that the temperature at which the vapor layer forms depends on the surface and liquid used.
questions.explanation: The assumption that collapse temperature varies with materials is refuted by the finding that it does not; C states this directly.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The United States has designated more than 500 areas National Wildlife Refuges (NWR).
  • Some NWRs were established specifically to protect endangered species.
  • The Crocodile Lake NWR is a 6,686-acre area in Florida.
  • It was established to protect the endangered American crocodile.
  • The Pearl Harbor NWR is a 61-acre area in Hawaii.
  • It was established to protect the endangered Hawaiian stilt.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two NWRs. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Both the Crocodile Lake NWR and the Pearl Harbor NWR were established to protect endangered species.
Some NWRs, such as Hawaii’s Pearl Harbor, were established specifically to protect endangered species.
While the Crocodile Lake NWR extends across a 6,686-acre area, the Pearl Harbor NWR encompasses only 61 acres.
The US has designated more than 500 areas as NWRs, including the Crocodile Lake NWR in Florida.
questions.explanation: Only A names a shared purpose of the two refuges.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • A supercontinent is a single landmass made up of most or all of Earth’s continents.
  • Over time, continents merge together to form supercontinents, which then break apart.
  • This process is believed to take hundreds of millions of years and is known as the supercontinent cycle.
  • Rodinia and Euramerica were supercontinents.
  • Rodinia formed about 1.1 billion years ago.
  • Euramerica formed about 300 million years ago.
questions.question: The student wants to correct a misunderstanding that Euramerica formed before Rodinia. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Rodinia and Euramerica were both supercontinents, single landmasses made up of most or all of the Earth’s continents.
Rodinia formed about 1.1 billion years ago, long before Euramerica’s formation about 300 million years ago.
Forming and breaking apart over hundreds of millions of years, supercontinents are made up of most or all of Earth’s continents.
Euramerica and Rodinia formed at different times in Earth’s history.
questions.explanation: Only B gives both dates, showing Rodinia formed first.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Niger River is the third longest river in Africa.
  • It ranks No. 14 among the longest rivers in the world.
  • It is 4,200 kilometers long.
  • The Indus River is the ninth longest river in Asia.
  • It ranks No. 19 among the longest rivers in the world.
  • It is 3,610 kilometers long.
questions.question: The student wants to emphasize the different locations of the two rivers. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: The Indus River is 3,610 kilometers long.
The Niger River is in Africa, whereas the Indus River is located in Asia.
The Niger River ranks No. 14 among the longest rivers in the world.
At 4,200 kilometers long, the Niger River is the third longest in Africa.
questions.explanation: Only B contrasts where the two rivers are.
